list: The official 55 trophies, as PlayStation publishes them (via Exophase / PSNProfiles, 2026-11-18).
note: Guides are written in the author's own words from the official descriptions. The game had not released when this guide was written, so no specific in-game location or step is claimed beyond what the official description states; anything drawn from earlier GTA games is labelled Series precedent (GTA V).

trophies.guide: This is the platinum trophy, and it unlocks automatically once you have earned the other 54 trophies, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Work through the roadmap in order: finish the story, sweep the collectibles, clear the activities, then mop up the missable and clean-up trophies last. Keep the checklist in this guide ticked as you go so nothing is left behind.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission Gone Fishing and see it through to its end; the trophy unlocks when the mission completes. This is the first story mission, so it cannot be missed — just follow the on-screen objectives as the game teaches you its controls. It is the natural first step of the platinum road.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1, in story order, until the chapter closes and this trophy pops. Chapter trophies are unmissable as long as you keep playing the story, so there is no special preparation. If a mission fails, replay it from the checkpoint or the mission replay menu until it is done.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 by finishing all of its story missions in order. Like the other chapter trophies it unlocks from story progress alone and cannot be missed. Use the time in this chapter to start learning the side systems — driving, shooting and the open world — because later trophies build on them.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its final mission and complete it; the trophy is awarded for finishing the chapter. It is story-locked and unmissable, so no side content is required. Keep an eye on the missable trophies in this guide while you play, because some partner and choice trophies can only be attempted while the story still allows them.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Finish all of Chapter 4's missions to earn this trophy; it marks the end of the chapter and is unmissable. By this point in the story you will have met most of the characters tied to the later contact trophies, so note who gives you missions. Nothing in this chapter needs to be done in a special order for the trophy itself.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the game's final story mission to earn this gold trophy; it is the story's endpoint and cannot be missed. Before you start the finale, consider finishing any partner-based or choice-based trophies first, because the story's availability of partners and choices narrows as the plot closes. Once the credits roll, the open world remains for collectibles and activities.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run; the trophy unlocks at the mission's end. Mission trophies like this one are unmissable as long as you play the story, so just follow the mission objectives. If you fail a section, retry it until the mission completes.
trophies.name: Trust
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist, a heist mission whose name promises a big score. Heist missions in the series usually involve planning and a set-piece escape, so expect a longer mission with several stages. The trophy is awarded on completion and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play to unlock this trophy. As with the other named-mission trophies, it is tied to story progress and unmissable. Play the mission when it appears in your story flow and finish it to move on.
trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners; the trophy pops when the mission ends. It is a story-progression trophy and cannot be missed. Keep playing the main story in order and it will come naturally.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. The trophy unlocks on mission completion and is unmissable. Note the airport location: the separate activity trophy about an unscheduled departure at VCIA is a different, free-roam challenge, not this mission.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory to earn this trophy. It is awarded for story progress and cannot be missed. The mission's name suggests a large-scale operation, so expect a demanding set-piece; retry from checkpoints if a section fails.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own completion tracker, which counts story missions, collectibles, activities and side content together. This is a late-game trophy by nature: finish the story, all collectibles and all activities first, then check the in-game stats to find what is still missing. Series precedent (GTA V): the 100% checklist there covered story, stranger missions, hobbies, collectibles and stunts, so expect a similar spread here — but the exact checklist for GTA VI is only confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts in total across the open world — jumps, near misses, long airtime and similar driving feats that the game counts as stunts. Stunts add up passively as you drive aggressively, but reaching 250 is faster if you deliberately chain jumps and risky driving between other tasks. Series precedent (GTA V): stunt jumps and airtime counted toward similar tallies there, so look for ramps and long straight roads; the exact stunt types GTA VI counts are confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers at least once — one race, one fishing trip, one arcade game, and so on through the full activity list. The official description does not give a number, so this guide does not claim one: use the in-game activities menu as your checklist and try each entry on it once. This is a good early trophy because it teaches you which activities you enjoy and which trophies they feed into.
trophies.name: Master of None
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Visit the shooting range, work through each challenge, and repeat any challenge until you hit the gold-medal score or time — bronze or silver on a challenge does not count. This is a skill trophy, so expect to replay the harder challenges; practise the weapon types you are weakest with first and save the toughest challenges for last.
trophies.name: The Shootist
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. Find the drone-race spots around Leonida, enter a race at each one, and finish first; a win at a location you have already won does not add a new one. Learn each course's turns before racing for the win, and retry a location as often as needed — races can be replayed.
trophies.name: Top Fun
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race counts once, so winning the same race again does not add to the total. Spread your wins across the race types the game offers (road races, drone races and any others on the activities list) until 20 distinct races are won. Races are replayable, so a lost race costs nothing but another attempt.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Take on Cal in a fishing challenge and beat him. Fishing challenges are an activity you can enter from the fishing spots; challenge Cal when the option appears and out-fish him within the challenge's rules. If you lose, challenge him again — the trophy only needs one win.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Find an arcade machine and play one arcade game through to completion. Any arcade game counts, so pick the one you find easiest and finish it. Arcades are part of the activities list, so this also counts toward trying each activity type.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Play through Andy's mission line until you complete his final mission; the trophy unlocks at its end. Contact missions appear as that character's missions become available in the story, so keep checking for Andy's missions between story chapters. This is story-gated but unmissable while his missions are still available.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission to earn this trophy. Work through Kenton's mission line in order as his missions unlock; the trophy is awarded for the last one. Like the other contact trophies it follows story availability, so do his missions when they appear rather than leaving them all to the end.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission line by completing his final mission. Billy's missions unlock as the story progresses, so play them when they appear. The trophy is tied to that final mission alone and is unmissable while the mission is available.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers met around Leonida — the series' classic Strangers & Freaks side missions, each a short chain of tasks for a stranger. Explore the map and watch for stranger markers; each completed strand counts once, so you need eight different ones. Some strands may only appear in certain story phases, so start them when you find them instead of saving them all for after the story.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission to earn this trophy. Play Randy's missions in order as they unlock during the story. It is a contact-progression trophy, unmissable while his missions remain available.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission; the trophy is awarded when that mission ends. Follow Tyrone's mission line as it unlocks in the story. Like the other contact trophies, it cannot be missed while his missions are still on offer.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Find and meditate at all 18 meditation spots spread across Leonida. Meditation spots are a collectible-style activity: visit each one and use the meditate prompt, and the game tracks how many you have done. No specific spot locations are confirmed before release — explore the map systematically, region by region, and tick spots off in this guide as you find them.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a specific animal tied to Bret's request, not just any wildlife. Take Bret's hunting task when it appears, track the animal it names, and bring it down. Hunting in the series usually means following tracks and using a quiet approach, so plan a careful hunt rather than a loud one; the exact animal and location are confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets by finding the cards scattered around Leonida and filling three sets. Cards are a collectible hunt: pick up every card you pass, and use the in-game collection view to see which sets are nearly complete so you can target the missing cards. This is a long grind best done alongside exploring the map for the other collectibles.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations across Leonida. WAiNK It is a photo-style activity at marked spots, so visit varied places — landmarks, viewpoints and districts — and use it once at each new spot until the count reaches 100. It pairs naturally with exploring all 52 areas for the exploration trophy, so do both sweeps together.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges in total — the game's general challenge list, separate from the 42 Shooting Range challenges. Work through the challenge menu steadily: driving, combat, exploration and activity challenges all count toward the same 50. Check the in-game challenge list regularly so you can pick off the easy ones first and leave the grindy ones for the clean-up stage.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level and then lose the police and escape. The key condition is your partner's presence: you must do this while your partner is with you, and partner availability is limited by the story, so attempt it during a story phase when your partner is available rather than after the finale. Lose the cops by breaking line of sight and hiding until the wanted level clears. MISSABLE: if no partner is available any more, the attempt cannot be made.
trophies.name: Hot Together
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, rob three shops in a row without letting your wanted level drop in between — the wanted level must be kept alive across all three robberies. Plan a route of three nearby shops, rob each quickly, and keep moving so the police stay engaged but do not catch you. This needs your partner with you, and partner availability is limited by the story, so do it while a partner is available. MISSABLE: without a partner at your side, the trophy cannot be attempted.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive, find or otherwise encounter 100 distinct vehicle types across Leonida. Variety is what counts, so try every vehicle class you meet: cars, bikes, boats, planes and anything unusual. Exploring new districts and vehicle-heavy areas (docks, airports, garages) helps; the in-game vehicle log shows what you have found so far.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Activate Combat Focus and take down 5 enemies before it ends — a single use must account for all five. Pick a fight with a group of enemies in the open, trigger Combat Focus when they are clustered, and chain your shots quickly. If you fall short, retry: the trophy only needs one successful run, so set up a favourable fight and try again.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — leave VCIA in a plane outside the normal flights. Get to the airport, take a plane, and take off without following a scheduled departure. This is a free-roam stunt, not a story mission, so you can attempt it any time you can reach the airfield; the exact method is confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: This trophy is tied to the Rhino tank — the official description is a joke line, so the exact trigger is not spelled out in the description itself. Series precedent (GTA V): Rhino-related trophies there involved using the tank, so expect to get into a Rhino and use it; the precise action GTA VI requires is confirmed only in-game. Check the in-game stats or trophy progress hint once you have a Rhino to see what it is tracking.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery. Plan the approach: enter quietly, avoid cameras and guards' sightlines, take the goods and leave before any alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting through it. The exact detection rules are confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault robbery counts once, and you must get away clean afterwards for it to count. Plan each robbery with an escape route in mind — a fast vehicle nearby and a route out of the police search area. Vaults are repeatable targets, so work through five of them across your playthrough.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape afterwards. Armored trucks roam the roads as moving targets: intercept one, stop it, take its cargo and get away before the police close in. Series precedent (GTA V): armored trucks there were stopped by blocking or ramming them, so expect a similar approach — but the exact method in GTA VI is confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida, from Vice City to the far corners of the state. Drive, fly or sail into every region until the exploration counter hits 52 — the in-game map shows which areas you have visited. Do this sweep alongside the meditation spots, the WAiNK It locations and the card hunt, since all of them reward thorough exploration.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs in Leonida. Find gang operations around the map, rob one per gang, and keep a note of which gangs you have hit — robbing the same gang twice does not add to the count. Gang territory is the clue to which gang an operation belongs to, so spread your robberies across different districts.
trophies.name: Pest Control
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy it with the view — a small moment trophy, not a challenge. Find the bar or vendor on Ocean Beach, buy the cocktail, and the trophy should pop when the scene plays. It is a clean-up trophy: easy, quick, and best saved for a relaxed moment between harder tasks.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Get into a vehicle showroom and smash your way out in it — drive a vehicle through the showroom's front in classic GTA style. Pick a showroom, take a vehicle, and break out through the glass; the trophy is about the spectacle, so a fast exit in a heavy vehicle is the idea. The exact showroom and trigger are confirmed only in-game.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl — follow through on a bowling game there. This is the bowling activity trophy, tied to that specific alley, so play at least one game at that location. It pairs with the bowling-related combat trophy, so you can practise your aim between frames.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: This trophy's official description is deliberately vague — a partnership moment with mass appeal — so the exact trigger is not spelled out in the description. It reads as a story or relationship beat involving your partner and a public moment, so it will most likely come from playing the story and partner content naturally. No specific step is claimed here because none is confirmed before release; play the partner storylines and it should surface.
trophies.name: Personal Best
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count of 500 choices for this trophy, so it is a long accumulation across the game, not a single decision. Choose dialogue options, story branches and activity decisions whenever they appear, and the count will climb over a full playthrough. MISSABLE in spirit: it is tied to story choices that can go one way only, so if a playthrough offers too few choice moments, the count may stall — keep choosing whenever the game offers a choice, and do not rush past dialogue options.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try — fail something, then succeed at the very next attempt. This is the classic retry trophy: it most likely triggers when you fail a mission, challenge or activity and then pass it on the immediate retry. If it does not pop naturally, deliberately fail a short, easy activity once and then pass it on the second attempt. MISSABLE in the sense that it is tied to a second-try moment: a flawless playthrough with no failed attempts would never trigger it, so do not fear an early failure.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the game's hidden or random weird event. This reads as a secret-moment trophy: something unusual in the open world that you have to be in the right place to see. No specific event is confirmed before release, so this guide claims none; explore odd corners of Leonida, visit strange landmarks at different times, and it should find you. Series precedent (GTA V): UFOs, ghosts and other easter eggs filled this role there.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
Series precedent (GTA V)

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a target, lean out with a melee weapon, and connect while the vehicle is moving. A quiet road with pedestrians is the place to try it; missing costs nothing, so keep attempting until one connects. It pairs with the bowling alley visit, since both are about bowling in different senses.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists; take them to your contacts to launder them into clean cash, and the total laundered counts toward $250,000. Keep laundering after every big score instead of spending dirty money directly, and the total will build steadily across the playthrough.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops — weapons, clothes, vehicles, food and anything else you buy all count toward the same total. This accumulates naturally over a full playthrough, especially once you start buying vehicles and property. If you are short near the end, buy and sell high-value items to push the total over the line; the count is cumulative spending, not money held.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties across Leonida. Garages are property you buy to store vehicles; find each one for sale, save up, and buy them all. This is a money trophy as much as a property one, so it pairs with the laundering and spending trophies — earn, launder, then spend on garages until all eight are yours.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game vehicle-sharing app. Find vehicles around Leonida, register each one through the app, and repeat until 10 are registered. Variety helps: register different vehicles you come across during exploration rather than the same one ten times. The app's own list shows how many you have registered so far.
trophies.name: On the Spot
sources: Official trophy description — PlayStation (via Exophase / PSNProfiles)
